title: Why Deere Stock Hit an All-Time High This Week
author: Howard Smith
description: Deere & Co. stock reached a record high above $700 per share this week, jumping 10% following a strong Q3 earnings report and a $250 million increase to full-year net income guidance. CEO John May indicated that 2026 will mark the bottom of the agricultural equipment cycle, signaling the start of a recovery. Analyst Mircea Dobre maintains a buy rating and projects the stock could reach $800, representing 15% upside potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 earnings, increased full-year net income guidance by $250 million, stock hit all-time high above $700, CEO signals 2026 as bottom of ag equipment cycle indicating recovery ahead, analyst maintains buy rating with $800 price target representing 15% upside potential.

title: KUBTY vs. DE: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two Manufacturing - Farm Equipment sector stocks, Kubota Corp. (KUBTY) emerges as the superior value option over Deere (DE). KUBTY holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with stronger earnings estimate revisions, while DE has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). KUBTY's valuation metrics are significantly more attractive, featuring a forward P/E of 12.03 versus DE's 37.31, a PEG ratio of 1.20 compared to DE's 2.79, and a P/B ratio of 1.12 versus DE's 6.51, earning KUBTY an A Value grade against DE's F grade.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: KUBTY demonstrates superior value characteristics with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), stronger earnings estimate revisions, lower forward P/E ratio (12.03), lower PEG ratio (1.20), lower P/B ratio (1.12), and an A Value grade, making it the recommended choice for value investors.

DE shows weaker value metrics with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), significantly higher forward P/E ratio (37.31), higher PEG ratio (2.79), higher P/B ratio (6.51), and an F Value grade, indicating it is overvalued relative to KUBTY.

title: Why Deere Stock Rallied Today
author: Joe Tenebruso
description: Deere stock rose 3.90% after analyst Mircea Dobre predicted a near-term recovery in the U.S. farming market driven by rising corn and soy prices. Dobre projects Deere's earnings per share will grow to $25 in 2027 and over $30 in 2028, upgrading his price target from $640 to $800, representing potential gains of over 22%.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Analyst upgrade with increased price target from $640 to $800 based on expected significant earnings growth driven by improving farm profitability from rising crop prices. Stock rallied 3.90% on the positive outlook.

title: CAT's Construction Revenues Up 35% in Q2: Can It Maintain This Pace?
author: Na
description: Caterpillar's Construction Industries segment is experiencing robust momentum with revenue increases exceeding 30% in Q1 and Q2 2026, driven by higher sales volumes and favorable pricing. The company is expanding digital, rental, and autonomous solutions while targeting a 1.25x increase in sales to end users by 2030. However, Caterpillar faces intensifying competition from Komatsu and Deere, which are pursuing similar automation and digitalization strategies.

title: Bill Gates' Foundation Holds Berkshire Hathaway as Its Top Stock, a Signal of Its Preference for Steady Compounders Over Flashy Tech
author: Lawrence Rothman, Cfa
description: The Gates Foundation Trust's $34.4 billion equity portfolio reveals a preference for industrial and consumer stocks over technology companies. With Berkshire Hathaway as its largest holding at $7.4 billion, the foundation also maintains significant positions in Caterpillar, Canadian National Railway, Waste Management, and Deere. This strategy demonstrates that solid long-term returns can be achieved through steady compounders rather than volatile tech stocks, while still benefiting from trends like AI-driven data center construction.
